questions.q: What single thread runs through every decision made in this nine-lesson project?
options: Each choice was the simplest option that still actually solved the problem — right-sized, not maximal
Every decision was made to showcase the most advanced Snowflake feature available
Every object was built exactly like the Advanced capstone's, with no adjustments
Each lesson added a new stakeholder to increase realism
questions.explain: XS warehouse, a view instead of a table, Import instead of DirectQuery, one role instead of a governance framework — all right-sized to a one-stakeholder project, not shortcuts.

questions.q: What specifically triggers the shift from this Beginner project's approach to the Intermediate project's approach?
options: A second stakeholder needing access to overlapping data, which breaks several of this project's one-stakeholder simplifications
Driftwood Media switching from Snowflake to a different data warehouse
The VP of Support being replaced by a new VP
Power BI being replaced by a different reporting tool
questions.explain: The whole arc of this capstone is built around when added complexity actually earns its place — and that's when a second stakeholder enters the picture.

questions.q: What does the Intermediate project replace the manual COPY INTO load with, once more than one person depends on fresh data?
options: A Streams-and-Tasks pipeline, so fresh data lands automatically instead of depending on someone remembering to run a load
A nightly phone call to the support team
Snowpipe, triggered by the VP's calendar invite
Nothing — manual loads continue regardless of stakeholder count
questions.explain: Once more than one person relies on fresh data, 'someone remembers to run the load' stops being a reliable process, which is exactly what Streams and Tasks solve.

questions.q: What stays exactly the same between this Beginner project and the Intermediate project that follows it?
options: The core discipline: clarify the real ask, name objects before building, grant only what's needed, and build the smallest thing that answers the question
The exact SQL syntax used in every query
The number of stakeholders involved
The warehouse size, regardless of workload
questions.explain: The underlying discipline this project taught is reusable even as the specific tools (roles, pipelines, data formats) scale up with more stakeholders.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what Snowflake feature handles semi-structured JSON data, which becomes relevant once richer source systems are involved?
options: The VARIANT data type, along with the FLATTEN function
The QUALIFY clause
AUTO_SUSPEND on the warehouse
The DRIFTWOOD_SUPPORT_ANALYST role
questions.explain: VARIANT stores semi-structured JSON inside a relational table, and FLATTEN converts it into a relational shape a view can summarize — covered in the main Snowflake course's Chapter 7.
